Near the pseudo-critical point, supercritical water undergoes large, continuous property changes without a phase-change latent heat: density drops sharply, specific heat capacity spikes to a peak (cp,max at the pseudo-critical temperature for a given pressure), thermal conductivity and viscosity vary strongly, and enthalpy rises rapidly with only modest temperature change. Because these effects are sensitive to local operating conditions and channel geometry, their onset and severity are design- and correlation-dependent, and no single heat transfer correlation reliably captures HTD across all SCWR operating ranges — this remains an active area of uncertainty in SCWR thermal-hydraulic design.
